title: Past tense: what happened
description: Talk about what you did, using regular verbs and the common irregular ones.

guide.title: Regular past: stem + id + ending (singular)
guide.text:
The past tense is the past stem + a personal ending. For the many regular verbs in -u, the past stem is the verb without its u, plus -id-: maadu - maadid-.

The singular endings are: -e (I), -e (you, familiar), -a (he), -lu (she), and -tu for 'it'.

naanu maadide and neenu maadide are identical; the pronoun tells them apart. For 'he', the short form maadida is what you say; the written form adds -nu: maadidanu. 'She' is maadidlu in speech and maadidalu (ಮಾಡಿದಳು) in writing. 'It' is maaditu (ಮಾಡಿತು).

Other regular verbs: nodu - nodide (I saw); kelu - kelide (I asked, heard); helu - helide (I said); maataadu - maataadide (I spoke); odu - odide (I read); torisu - toriside (I showed).

guide.title: Plural and respectful forms
guide.text:
The plural endings in speech are: -vi (we), -ri (you, polite or plural), -ru (they / respectful he or she). So: maadidvi, maadidri, maadidru.

The written forms have an extra vowel: maadidevu (ಮಾಡಿದೆವು) we did; maadidiri (ಮಾಡಿದಿರಿ) you did; maadidaru (ಮಾಡಿದರು) they did. The neuter plural is maadidavu in both.

Since respected people take the plural, 'Father said' is appa helidru.

examples.english: They did. / He or she did. (respectful; written: maadidaru)

guide.title: Irregular past stems to learn by heart
guide.text:
The commonest verbs have irregular past stems. The endings are the regular ones; only the stem and the 'it' form must be memorised. Each line gives: I, he, she, it, we, you (polite), they.

ಹೋಗು hogu (go) - stem hod-: hode, hoda, hodlu, hoytu, hodvi, hodri, hodru.
ಬಾ baa (come) - stem band-: bande, banda, bandlu, bantu, bandvi, bandri, bandru.
ತಿನ್ನು tinnu (eat) - stem tind-: tinde, tinda, tindlu, tintu, tindvi, tindri, tindru.
ಕುಡಿ kudi (drink) - stem kudid-: kudide, kudida, kudidlu, kudiyitu, kudidvi, kudidri, kudidru.
ಕೊಡು kodu (give) - stem kott-: kotte, kotta, kotlu, kottitu, kotvi, kotri, kotru.
ಇರು iru (be) - stem idd-: idde, idda, idlu, ittu, idvi, idri, idru.
ಆಗು aagu (become, happen) - stem aad-: aade, aada, aadlu, aaytu, aadvi, aadri, aadru.

The 'you, familiar' form is always the same as the 'I' form: neenu hode, neenu bande.

Written forms keep the dropped vowel: hodalu, hoyitu, hodevu, hodiri, hodaru; bandalu, banditu, bandevu, bandiri, bandaru; kottalu, kottevu, kottiri, kottaru; iddalu, iddevu, iddiri, iddaru; aayitu.

More irregular pasts you will meet soon: nillu (stand, stop) - ninte; kootko (sit) - kootkonde; tago (take) - tagonde; elu (get up) - edde; beelu (fall) - bidde; kali (learn) - kalite; bare (write) - barede; mare (forget) - marete; sigu (be found, be got) - sikkitu.

guide.title: The neuter past and 'it happened'
guide.text:
The neuter ('it') forms are the least regular and the most used, because weather, time, work, events and things are all neuter.

ಆಯ್ತು (aaytu) 'it happened, it is done' - written ಆಯಿತು (aayitu). kelasa aaytu, 'the work is done'; oota aaytu, 'the meal is over (I have eaten)'.
ಹೋಯ್ತು (hoytu) 'it went, it is gone' - written ಹೋಯಿತು (hoyitu).
ಬಂತು (bantu) 'it came' - written ಬಂದಿತು (banditu). male bantu, 'it rained'.
ಇತ್ತು (ittu) 'it was, there was'. chali ittu, 'it was cold'.
ಸಿಕ್ಕಿತು (sikkitu) 'it was found, (I) got it'.

The negative past is the same for all persons and all verbs: stem + -alilla (baralilla, 'didn't come'; sigalilla, 'didn't get'). 'There was not' is ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ (iralilla).

phrases.note: maadide + y + aa. In fast speech: maadidyaa? (ಮಾಡಿದ್ಯಾ?). Polite: neevu oota maadidraa? (ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ?)

phrases.english: I was there for two years.
phrases.note: No word for 'for' is needed with a length of time.
ittu is the neuter past of iru.
sigu = to be found, to be available; the person is in the dative.
